subject: Renewal checkpoint: ReefAI usage health, tranche reallocation & burst plan

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 renewal check-in + usage snapshot

Hi Lauren,

Hope you’re well — ReefAI’s renewal is coming up mid-October and I wanted to get a quick, pragmatic read on where we stand from a usage/health perspective. Our CFO is asking for a concise summary of: token burn trends, any sustained latency/QUality regressions post-July rollout, and options if we want to shift some of our committed volume into a staged uplift rather than a single-step increase.

We pulled together a short list of asks:
- A one-page health scorecard we can show execs (tokens, 95p latency, error rate)
- A proposal for a tranche reallocation (move 20% of current headroom into burst credits for holiday traffic)
- Any evidence of model drift / quality declines on recent LLM mix changes

Attaching our internal usage extract for August to help the review. Could we book 30 minutes next week to walk through?

Thanks — Evan
Evan Park
Customer Success, ReefAI

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 renewal check-in + usage snapshot

Evan — thanks for the data and the clear asks. We can absolutely get you a concise health scorecard and a tranche-based uplift plan. High-level notes before a call:

- Token trends: August spike (you highlighted) looked concentrated around a single feature rollout; daily 7-day average jumped 42% and then normalized over two weeks.
- Latency/Errors: 95p latency remained within SLA for the most part, but we did see elevated p99 during a 24h window on 2027-08-09 tied to a model variant routing mismatch (we rolled a hotfix same day). Error rate stayed under 0.6%.
- Quality: small regression (measured on your eval set) against the new opt-quant model on short-context prompts (~1.7% decline on intent accuracy). We have mitigation options (prefetching + fallback to float model on problematic routes).

Proposal we’d like to review on the call:
1) Scorecard PDF (one page) with token burn, 95/99 latency, error %, and quality delta — we’ll share a draft before the meeting.
2) Tranche reallocation: move 20% of unused committed units into a burst-credit pool that auto-consumes on region-level surge, with a 90-day reconciliation window.
3) Canary flow: we recommend a 2-week canary (10% traffic) on the quantized variant for your most latency-sensitive endpoints, with automatic rollback criteria.

I’ll loop in Ben (sales) for pricing/commit sizing and Karthik for SLA/ops patterns. Proposed times: Thu 9/16 11:00 or Fri 9/17 10:00 PT — would either work?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Q4 renewal checkpoint: ReefAI usage health, tranche reallocation & burst plan

Forwarding the thread — quick notes for the proposed commercial approach:
- If ReefAI wants the burst-credit pool (20% of unused commitment) with a 90-day reconciliation, we can map it to a staged uplift addendum: 6-month tranche with a step-up pricing matrix (0-50% burst = base; 50-100% = +7%).
- Option: provide one complimentary 30-day burst top-up (up to 10% of committed tokens) if they sign a 12-month renew/expand by Oct 15. Helps close with CFO.

Karthik — are there any operational constraints you need on the burst auto-consume rules (region pinning / model fallbacks)?

Ben
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q4 renewal checkpoint: ReefAI usage health, tranche reallocation & burst plan

Looping in Monica from Solutions so we can pin the technical guardrails. Quick ops constraints:
- Burst credits: can be region-scoped (we recommend us-west primary + us-east fallback) and tied to a model-class (e.g., quantized variants only) to control cost.
- Auto-consume policy: trigger when 95p latency crosses configured SLO for >10 minutes AND token throughput > 150% of baseline for the minute.
- Rollback criteria: if error rate >1.2% for 10 minutes, or if quality delta on sampled requests >3% decline vs baseline, auto-backoff to reserved capacity.

Monica — can you prepare a short Ops play (runbook + alert thresholds) for the call so we can include it in the MAP?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
